request.spec: Exports taken while a preview date is set use the preview figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Exports taken while a preview date is set use the preview figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I made no code changes because the app already does what the request asks. The first `bin/e2e` run, on the untouched code, passed all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts`. That includes the main test, which sets a preview of 2026-05-01 and expects the people and claims exports to show 11.00 instead of 10.00, then 10.00 again after clearing it.

It already works because:
- **The server reads the preview date.** While a preview is set, every read request sends it in the `X-Preview` header. `PreviewDate.java` then works out figures as if the sheet's today were that date, while changes still use the real today.
- **The exports are built on the page from that data.** The people, claims and statement exports (`people.ts:2179–2216`) wait for the latest read and use the same values and date the screen shows. So they match whatever the screen is displaying, preview included.
- **The pools export re-reads first.** `exportPools` (`pools.ts:279`) fetches the pools again before writing the file, and that request also carries the preview header.

I didn't edit any files or add any audit records, since nothing needed changing. If you expected some export to behave differently under a preview than this, tell me which one and I'll look again.
